sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: As of the Nov 13 close, the S&P 500 sits at 7,562, roughly mid-range in its one-month band of 7,354 to 7,757 and about 2% below where the window began. The Nasdaq 100 is weaker, at 27,944 versus a 29,951 start (−6.7%) and in the lower half of its range. The Euro Stoxx 50 is the contrast, at 6,387 and within a point of its monthly high. The VIX closed at 19.3, up from 15.3 a month ago after a peak of 28.2. The week carries 39 scheduled reports in the tracked universe, concentrated in consumer-cyclical (10 names) and technology (9), with 23 landing Thursday.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: The three leading sectors by recent reaction (energy, copper, mining) have no names reporting this week, so the calendar leans on mid-table sectors. Tue: Home Depot (HD US) reports into consumer-cyclical, median +0.4% off recent prints, while Disney (DIS US) plugs into communication-services, roughly flat at −0.1%. Wed: Target (TGT US) reports into consumer-defensive at −0.3% median, and Palo Alto Networks (PANW US) into technology at +0.2%. Thu is the heaviest day: Kroger (KR US) joins consumer-defensive and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD US) joins communication-services. All 39 dates are still estimates, not company-confirmed.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Energy leads the reaction table at +1.9% median across 315 tickers, with 5,031 news items, a thick window. Copper follows at +1.7% on only 6 tickers and 228 items, so it is a thin sample. Mining matches it at +1.7% across 215 tickers and 2,763 items. Nothing in the sectors reporting this week is moving more than half a percent at the median, so this week's prints have little recent sector momentum to lean on.
